[34mInvestigated:[0m Traced the read and write paths in tinydb/storages.py and tinydb/table.py: JSONStorage keeps one open handle, read() re-parses the whole file on each call, _read_table() and _update_table() each call storage.read(), and writes go through the same handle. Ran the 40 MB benchmark and the full test suite with pytest.ini bypassed. A standalone check script (/tmp/t_cache.py) exercised cache hits, external rewrites, mtime-preserving rewrites, and a failing updater. The initial pytest run failed because pytest.ini passes coverage flags that the installed pytest does not accept.

[33mLearned:[0m JSONStorage.read() re-parsed the full file on every call, which made each uncached search almost entirely parse time. A parse cache keyed on inode, size, mtime, and ctime detects external rewrites, including ones that restore the old mtime, because ctime still changes. Files modified within the last 2 seconds are not cached, which guards against timestamp-granularity races. The cached object is shared with callers, and an updater that fails partway can leave the cache partially modified unless invalidated. Document construction in db.all() is unaffected by the parse cache.

[32mCompleted:[0m Added a parse cache to JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py, with a signature check, a 2-second settle window, invalidation in write() and close(), and a public invalidate_cache() method. Added cache invalidation in Table._update_table() in tinydb/table.py when an updater raises. The 228-test suite passes with pytest.ini bypassed. The benchmark shows an uncached search dropping from about 465 ms to about 39 ms and db.all() from about 822 ms to a median of about 313 ms on the synthetic 43.9 MB database. The changes are not committed, and no new tests have been added.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The session is at a checkpoint. The open questions are whether to commit the cache changes and whether to add tests for the invalidation cases: external in-place rewrite, mtime-preserving rewrite, failed updater, and the settle window. The pytest.ini coverage-flag problem still needs a fix for the normal test command.

[36mNotes:[0m Two caveats remain. Cached read() results are shared objects, so mutating nested values in a returned document would corrupt later reads. If the importer replaces the file by rename rather than rewriting it in place, the open handle keeps pointing at the old inode, so read() would need to stat the path and reopen. Both caveats predate this change except that the cache makes the shared-object issue more consequential. The benchmark and test results come from one machine and one run.
